findings.file: CHANGELOG.md:70-73; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (the _units paragraph, 'a start beside a re-recorded red-first proof is two clean merges'); tests/test__manifest_merge.py wv27 (third 'apart' shape)
findings.issue: The shipped prose says a task's start beside a re-recorded red-first proof merges clean. It does so only when the start moves no status (a retry that bumps attempts and startedAt). A start in the ordinary sense moves status pending to in_progress, and then _units joins the close row (it shares `status`) because both sides changed it: I ran merge3 read-only on base pending, ours {status:in_progress, startedAt, attempts:1}, theirs {redFirst:{status:proved}} and it returned ONE conflict, tasks[P7.1].{status,startedAt,attempts,redFirst}. wv27 and the docs use a fixture whose status stays in_progress on all three sides, so the case never shows the plain start the sentence names. The behaviour is conservative (a conflict, never a mixed record), so this is a false claim in CHANGELOG, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and layout-adjacent prose, not a data hazard.
findings.resolution: Either narrow the sentence to 'a retry that moves no status' in CHANGELOG.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and add a wv27 fixture with a start that moves status expecting one conflict, or change the rows so a start does not pull in the close row through `status` alone.

findings.issue: The cost of the added cases is not measured or recorded. The task's recorded gate run (repeatedRun.durationMs 273991, 'machine to itself') took about 274 s for the four gate files; the red-first helper's fixed-tree run was still going at 114 s; sweep-costs.json holds 20.0 for test_merge_manifest.py and 0.2 for test__manifest_merge.py, and the sweep's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT floor is 300 s. rr1-rr10 build about eight real git repositories with the driver installed, and wv23/wv25 parse every .py under scripts/ and walk the schema about twenty times. I did not time the files singly, so which one holds the 274 s is not shown; what is shown is that the recorded costs no longer describe these files and the gate sits within about 10 percent of the per-job floor on this host, and CI runners (windows git is slower) are not this host.
findings.resolution: Time each file with the sweep's loud form, move rr1-rr10 into a block of their own if one file now dominates, and re-record .github/sweep-costs.json (--record-costs) so the hang detector is calibrated to the new cases rather than to the old ones.

intent.note: Clause (1) 'a value that is one account of one event merges whole ... in one table the merge reads and a case holds to the schema': MERGE_UNITS (_manifest_merge.py) names whole/container/map per kind, _merge_whole makes both-sides-changed one conflict, wv14-wv16 walk the schema and fail on an object value no row names; the run record and pointer, CI, merge stamp with head, sign-off verdict, review verdict are whole rows; the base-red record and base runs sit under $defs/lastRun/properties/baseRed in the schema, so they are whole with the run, and wv17 holds that the walk never reaches into a run. Clause (2) one side only is that side's value whole: _merge_whole returns the changed side. Clause (3) resolver: merge-manifest.py _foreign_records/_foreign_lines add the file and record path to both existing refusals (stray and no-id), counting the renumbered side; the refusal itself was already unconditional, so the diff adds the naming rather than a new refusal, which is what the clause asks ('the way it refuses an answer that differs from git's'). Clause (4): wv1 (red/green/newer red), wv4 (a key added on one side), wv5 (record deleted), wv6 (same run both sides), wv8, and rr1-rr3 through a real git merge with the installed driver. The 'what it cannot see' clause is stated in the module docstring, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and CHANGELOG. The executor's outcome describes the diff: MERGE_UNITS/ELEMENT_KINDS/REF_KINDS, _units, the split task and finding rows, the bug row without notes, render's one-block change, _foreign_records. One claim in the shipped docs overreaches the code (finding 1). Dependants: layout.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md are updated; tests/test__proposals.py and merge-manifest.py use merge3 and the parked-phase change is declared (wv22). render now makes every conflict one block, not only these, and CHANGELOG says so.
